description: Analyze spin density of the clean rutile MnO2 (110) surface.
user_prompt: Perform spin density analysis on the clean MnO2 (110) surface (rutile structure, P4_2/mnm). Determine whether the system has unpaired electrons. If unpaired electrons are present, identify the element carrying the spin density and report the magnetic moment of the outermost (undercoordinated, five-fold) surface-layer metal atom; otherwise report that there is no spin-carrying element and report the maximum residual site magnetic moment.

references: Tompsett, Parker & Islam, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 136, 1418 (2014)
Tompsett, Middlemiss & Islam, Phys. Rev. B 86, 205126 (2012)
method.modeling: Rutile beta-MnO2 (P4_2/mnm) non-polar, stoichiometric (110) surface (O-terminated); 4-5 layer slab with the bottom layers fixed, vacuum >= 15 A. AFM ground state: initialise alternating MAGMOM signs on Mn. Cleaving exposes a five-fold-coordinated surface Mn whose reduced coordination enhances its moment above the bulk-like six-fold Mn.
method.rationale: Clean rutile beta-MnO2 is an AFM insulator: every Mn is Mn4+ (3d3, S=3/2) and carries a local moment, so the spin-carrying element is Mn. Value from Tompsett et al. 2014: the undercoordinated five-fold surface Mn has a moment of 3.75 uB, enhanced above bulk Mn (3.09 uB) because reduced coordination lowers covalent quenching. Tompsett et al. 2012 documents the anisotropic FLL +U scheme needed for the correct AFM-insulating ground state (the effective-U approach gives a spurious FM metal for the parameter settings tested in that comparison). Tolerance 0.30 uB covers U-scheme and integration-sphere sensitivity.
